correctness.rationale: The proof is universal: cyclic run-window sums are bounded by the sorted largest/smallest sums after decomposing arbitrary lengths into whole periods plus a distinct-element remainder. The first t ones of the sorted word therefore span no more positions than any t successive ones in any rearrangement. Every length-n factor with t ones fits that sorted prefix, hence the exact inequality for all k>=1 and n>=0. Both sides coincide on the canonical rearrangement. The standalone checker passed 516 exhaustive profiles, 4368 arrangement pairs, 2896 positional profiles, and 1440 randomized larger cases; finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: This is a natural extremal problem motivated by prefix-normal forms and jumbled indexing. One explicit construction solves it simultaneously at every window length over independently variable run orders and gives a closed formula for arbitrary period and run multisets. A concrete strict example distinguishes it from vacuous prefix normality. No substantial downstream theorem or publication-sized claim is needed for the structural value.
